case_title: Manoj Kumar v. State of Himachal Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304 Part-II and 302; s.147 and 148
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of offences under s.302, 341 and 323 r/w.149 and ss.147 and 148
high_court_outcome: Acquitted 4 persons but confirmed conviction of other 3 accused-appellants
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and the deceased were involved in a land dispute. The deceased and others were returning to their village from a nearby village when they encountered the accused on disputed land. The accused, armed with weapons, suddenly attacked the deceased. The deceased was taken to a health center, where he was later declared dead. The deceased sustained two injuries, one of which was fatal later due to hemorrhage. The accused were convicted of various offences, including culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The High Court acquitted some accused but confirmed the conviction of others. The Supreme Court held that the accused did not have the intention to cause death, and the offence fell under Section 304 Part II of the IPC.
